faqs.question: What is MDes course?
faqs.answer: You may already know that MDes stands for Master of Design. It is a postgraduate specialised design degree programme. You can pursue MDes if you have a passion for the arts and want to excel in the design industry. MDes can be the best suited degree for you if you have deep interest in the artistic sector and who desire to acquire the ultimate standard in the area of design. The admissions process and fees for Master of Design programmes differ from university to university. The cost of a master's degree in design varies from university to university. Private universities may charge a little higher tuition fee for MDes admission, whilst government colleges may charge very little. An MDes degree course can be completed between INR 2 to INR 10 lakh. Some colleges require entrance tests, while others accept students based on their high school scores.

faqs.question: Why should I pursue MDes program?
faqs.answer:
A Master of Design degree is the gateway to specialisation and research as it is an advanced degree to conquer the Fashion and Design Industry in different disciplines such as Craft, Textiles, Special Needs, Publications, Media, Lifestyle Products, Graphics, and User Experience Design .

• The scope of a Master of Design degree is huge as it opens opportunities in various streams such as Industrial Engineering and Design, Product Research Analyst, Communication Design, Product Design, and Engineering, Visual Design, Animation, and Automotive Designing .
• Every day, the world of design evolves, and as a result, the demand for motivated and creative designers grows. During this degree, students will have the opportunity to work on assignments that will provide them with hands-on experience working in design studios .
• The aspirants of MDes can get find better job opportunities after MDes and enhance their pay scale. The programme prepares individuals to become entrepreneurs after completing the course or having appropriate skills. Following the conclusion of the course, many graduates have launched their own clothing lines.

faqs.question: Is an MDes course without a BDes worth it?
faqs.answer:
Definitely, to pursue an MDes program, BDes is not a mandatory criterion hence, even if you have not graduated with a BDes degree, fulfilling the basic eligibility criteria will get you a seat in the MDes program, and the same goes for the career scope.
However, depending on the MDes specialisation you choose, you should have a relevant bachelor's degree, for instance, if you wish to go for MDes in Interior, Web, or UI/UX Design, you must obtain a bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture , etc.

faqs.question: Can I become a Designer without pursuing MDes?
faqs.answer: Hi, yes, it's possible to become a Designer without opting for an MDes program . However, you'll need to fulfill the criteria set by the organisation you seek employment from. For example, if they require having a bachelor's degree in a specific discipline, you must fulfill the requirements. Also, creating a strong portfolio to attract high-paying jobs and projects is also important. You can also gain experience from internships and apprenticeship programs.

faqs.question: Which is better among MBA and MDes?
faqs.answer: Both the MBA (Master of Business Administration) and the MDes (Master of Design) courses are poles apart. An MBA is focused on business and management roles, polishing skills like finance, marketing, and strategy. Whereas, an MDes is focused on creativity and design disciplines.

full_content.text: Candidates seeking admission to design courses offered by the IITs , NIDs , or NIFTs must know that the admission process in these colleges is multi-tiered. Stage 1 of most design entrance exams is a written test. Shortlisted candidates must appear in a Studio/Situation Test that will evaluate their creativity and ability to handle different materials. In the case of PG courses, the Studio Test is typically followed by a Personal Interview . The prospect of appearing in a Personal Interview is daunting for many candidates. Also, there is no pre-defined formula as to what questions the jury may ask. So, preparing for the Personal Interview can be tricky. So, here we bring a few tips that candidates would find handy when facing the interview round for NIFT Entrance Exam , NID Entrance Exam , and CEED.
Design Admission Process

Most design entrance exams have a design aptitude test (DAT) that tests the design aptitude of the candidate. The NID DAT 2026 has the DAT Prelims and DAT Mains. The National Institute of Design (NID) conducted the DAT Prelims exam on January 5, 2025. On the day of the exam, the candidate had to bring their admit card and a valid photo ID proof. The NIFT 2025 entrance exam was conducted on February 9, 2025.
10 Tips to Crack Interview for Design Entrance Exam
The ten expert tips to ace your Design Entrance Interview are as follows:
1. Be on time

items: Make it a point to reach the venue where your interview is to be conducted (or log in to the system, in case of an online interview) on time. You may also visit your interview venue a day before the exam and do a recce on travel time, traffic situation, and the surrounding environment. However, if that is not possible, then make sure that you get the directions to the venue a day before.
Also, a good practice is to reach your interview venue at least 15 minutes before the scheduled time for your interview.

full_content.text: 2. Maintain etiquettes

items: It’s important to maintain a respectful and formal attitude during your interview. Avoid casual greetings such as "Hi" or even "Hello." Instead, opt for a polite and appropriate greeting like “Good morning” or “Good afternoon.”

When you enter the interview room, greet all the panelists courteously and ask for permission to be seated. Make sure your mobile phone is turned off; if that’s not possible, at least set it to silent mode to avoid any distractions.
Address the interviewers respectfully using “Sir,” “Ma’am,” or “Madam,” and always maintain a polite tone, regardless of the situation. Avoid interrupting, arguing, or responding rudely.
At the end of the interview, thank the panelists for their time, offer a polite farewell, and leave the room gracefully.

full_content.text: 3. Dress appropriately

items: Although there is no set dress code to appear for the interview round for admission in design courses offered at NIFT , NID , IIT Bombay , IIT Delhi , IISc Bangalore , IIT Guwahati , IIT Kanpur and IIT Hyderabad . However, it is advisable to wear formal clothes.
Also, pay special attention to the footwear you wear. Wearing chappals or any other casual footwear for an admission interview is a strict No-No.

full_content.text: 4. Do not use Slangs

Under no circumstances should you use slang like ‘you guys’, ‘OMG’, ‘cool’, ‘kinda’, ‘what’s up’, ‘awesome’, etc. If you utter any such words, chances are the jury may take offense. An interview is an extremely formal event, and you should make sure that you keep it that way.
5. Maintain eye contact

Try maintaining eye contact with the interviewers, this shows that you are confident and are well-aware of the questions put before you. However, make sure that you are not staring and simply conveying the fact that you are extremely interested in appearing for and clear the interview.
6. Carry your Portfolio

The panelists would be very interested in going through your work, and this will give you an added advantage because most likely, on viewing your portfolio, the entire interview would be conducted on how and why you created the different works mentioned in your portfolio.
Know how to create your portfolio for design course admissions by viewing the 5 Tips to prepare your portfolio for the CEED and NID Entrance Exam .
7. Do your homework

A little research on the college and course that you are applying for will always come in handy. You can do this research on the internet. This effort put in by you will prove helpful as it will reflect to your interviewers that you are interested in securing admission to the college.

full_content.text: 9. Know your subject

Most of the interviews for design course admissions revolve around testing the candidate’s aptitude and ability for the design stream they have selected to pursue. So, here it is advisable to be thorough in the subject of your preference, read about popular personalities in your field of choice, and develop a brief outline of what your expectations are of pursuing the course opted for.
10. Do not know the answer, admit it

If you have a subject question wherein you do not have any clue of the answer, admit your ignorance very frankly. Do not bluff or beat around the bush. Simply, inform the interviewers that you do not know the answer. If you are confident enough, you can ask the interviewer for guidance on where you can learn more about the topic, thus showing your curiosity about the subject.

However, if that is not possible, then make sure that you get the directions to the venue a day before.

It’s important to maintain a respectful and formal attitude during your interview. Avoid casual greetings such as "Hi" or even "Hello." Instead, opt for a polite and appropriate greeting like “Good morning” or “Good afternoon.”

When you enter the interview room, greet all the panelists courteously and ask for permission to be seated. Make sure your mobile phone is turned off; if that’s not possible, at least set it to silent mode to avoid any distractions.
Address the interviewers respectfully using “Sir,” “Ma’am,” or “Madam,” and always maintain a polite tone, regardless of the situation. Avoid interrupting, arguing, or responding rudely.
At the end of the interview, thank the panelists for their time, offer a polite farewell, and leave the room gracefully.

answers.answer_text: Aspirants must complete graduation from any discipline or field of study with a minimum of 50% aggregate to apply for MDes programme at GLS Institute of Design. questions.question_text: Does GLS Institute of Design offer Integrated MDes programme?

answers.answer_text: GLS Institute of Design offers a five-year Integrated BDes-MDes programme at the UG level. The programme is divided into 10 semesters. In the first year, students learn about fundamental design concepts. The next four years is for specialised study in Fashion Design, Communication Design, Product Design and Environment Design.

questions.question_text: What is the course structure of MDes at GLS Institute of Design?

answers.answer_text: GLS Institute of Design offers MDes for two-years in full-time mode. The course is divided into four semesters. During the first three semesters, students are involved in coursework at the institute. The final semester is for the MDes final project.

questions.question_text: Which are the MDes specialisations offered at GLS Institute of Design?

answers.answer_text: GLS Institute of Design offers MDes for two-years at the PG level. Candidates who have completed their graduation can apply for MDes in: Visual Communication Design Design Management Furniture & Retain Space Design
